evals.prompt: I rebased my personal feature branch onto the latest main, and now `git push` is rejected because the remote branch and my local branch have diverged. Give me the exact command to update the remote branch.
assertions: Recommends `git push --force-with-lease` (not plain `git push --force` or `git push -f`)
Does not suggest force-pushing to main/master

evals.prompt: I'm currently working inside a worktree whose directory is named `services`. Set up an isolated sibling worktree with its own branch so I can build a feature called `auth-fix` without touching my current checkout. Show the exact commands.
assertions: Creates a worktree directory named `services-feature-auth-fix` and a branch named `services/feature/auth-fix`
Records the source/base branch in a `branch.<branch>.mergeBackTo` git config value
Defaults to previewing the exact commands and effects unless apply was explicitly requested

evals.prompt: The only change staged in my repo is a version bump in `package.json` plus the matching update in `package-lock.json`. Write me the commit message.
assertions: The commit subject begins with the `chore:` type prefix
The subject is a single lowercase `<type>: <description>` line with no footer/trailer lines

evals.prompt: I added `config/local.env` to `.gitignore`, but git still keeps showing it as a tracked/modified file. How do I make git stop tracking it while keeping the file on disk?
assertions: Instructs to run `git rm --cached config/local.env` (removes from the index without deleting the working-tree file)

evals.prompt: Preview merging the feature worktree back to its recorded source branch. Do not change refs or clean anything up.
assertions: Resolves exact feature and source worktrees, branches, and revisions and reports the rebase, merge strategy, validation, and recovery commands
Does not merge, rebase, remove the worktree, or delete local or remote branches

evals.prompt: Abandon this failed feature worktree because the API assumption was wrong. Preserve enough information to resume or recover it.
assertions: Returns the reason, branch, HEAD revision, dirty-state summary, recovery command, and any unpushed or untracked risk
Does not commit, tag, reset, push, remove the worktree, or delete a branch

evals.prompt: Preview cleanup of stale feature worktrees older than 30 days. Show exactly what would be removed.
assertions: Treats age and naming as candidate signals, resolves exact worktree and ref targets, and protects dirty, active, unmerged, or unpushed work
Returns exact commands and recovery revisions without deleting anything; force and remote deletion require separate explicit authorization
